attachments.function: Front-mounted or mid-mounted between the front and rear wheels. Usable as a grader for leveling terrain, for pushing feed and grass back in the stable, or for cleaning silos.
Trencher for digging wet buffer strips and drainage ditches, so standing water is carried off the field efficiently.
Compact cultivator for soil cultivation in vegetable gardens and light plots.
Hoeing unit with single-axis (left/right) guidance that stays tightly between the rows, for example in maize, so weeds are cut close to the crop without damaging it.
Mechanical weed control using rotating fingers in light soil.

Front-mounted boom with conventional high-pressure nozzles that atomise the liquid into a fine mist. Each nozzle is switched individually, so only the detected weed is treated while the fine droplets fully cover the leaf surface. Based on the 'Open Weed Locator' project and ideal for contact herbicides and crop protection products.

Boom with individually controlled injectors that fire single coarse droplets on demand at low pressure. Every droplet is placed straight onto the weed, which practically eliminates drift and cuts chemical usage to a fraction of a conventional spray pass.

Two-axis system with CNC movement (left/right and up/down) carrying a drill that grinds individual weeds out of the sward. Developed for tap-rooted weeds such as broad-leaved dock, fully chemical-free.
Improving soil structure and air supply in grassland.
Mowing at various heights, including 'topping' plants above ground level.
Flexible arm with a brush cutter head or blades for mowing under fences and around obstacles.
Pumping water from ditches for local irrigation or crop spraying.
Precise application and spreading of granular fertilizers.
Spreading lime to improve soil pH levels and structure.
Seed box for initial crop sowing and for overseeding existing grassland in one pass.
Front-mounted unit that takes seedlings out of the tray and sets them out at the right spacing.
Compact seeder that spreads grass seed onto bare patches in the sward, so damaged spots close up again quickly.
Even distribution of sawdust or bedding material in stables.
Evenly spreading straw, specially designed for use between vegetable rows.
Transporting compost within the frame structure and spreading it between the crop rows.
Additional power supply modules to be installed between the frames.
Generator or combustion engine mounted between the frame as an auxiliary power source for extra electricity or mechanical power.
Integrated panels to extend battery life and provide sustainable power during operation.
Electric motors such as the Ego Power+ or Greenworks units to drive implements that need real power, replacing small petrol engines.
Large front-mounted brush or electrically driven radial brush for surface cleaning, as an alternative to the front push blade.
Front or rear-mounted seat, with the option to widen the frame tubes at the sides.
Motorized wheelbarrow-style bin for transporting and dumping loose materials, also usable as a carrying aid or mini dumper.
Rear-mounted hitch for pulling trailers and other rolling equipment.
Ballast weights to improve traction and vehicle balance for heavy tasks.
External hydraulic power source for applications where hydraulics are a better option than electricity.
Standard lifting system for attaching various agricultural implements.
Protective enclosure or housing for the operator.
Measuring grass and crop height and health to create task maps for nitrogen or phosphate.
Measuring and mapping soil density at specific data points.

Near-infrared sensor that measures the NDVI of the crop while driving. From the difference between reflected red and near-infrared light the robot reads biomass, ground cover and crop vitality, and builds live task maps for variable-rate fertilisation. Because the sensor moves close over the crop instead of looking down from a satellite, the readings stay reliable under cloud cover and also register small spots and gaps.

The robot works together with a drone as a mobile base station. The drone flies out from the platform, maps the plot from above and passes its imagery straight to the robot, which converts it into a driving and treatment plan. The drone charges and swaps batteries on the robot, so the pair can keep scouting and working alternately for a full day without anyone coming out to the field.

Several Bruut units work the same field as one swarm. The job is split into sections, the robots divide the passes among themselves and keep each other informed of position, progress and battery state, so they never overlap or cross. Capacity scales simply with the number of units instead of with machine size, work continues when one unit drops out, and the light platforms keep soil compaction low.
